seoTitle: How to Connect Vantage Broker to TradingView Charts
metaDescription: Link your Vantage trading account to TradingView to trade directly from the chart. Learn to authorize access, connect demo or live accounts, and fix errors.
intro: Trading straight from a TradingView chart is faster than bouncing between your broker's platform and your charting software, and Vantage — the broker formerly known as VantageFX — is one of the options TradingView lets you link directly. Once the two are connected, you can see your live balance in the corner of the chart, place trades against candles you're already looking at, and keep your account in sync without opening a second tab. The process is short, but the steps aren't obvious the first time: Vantage isn't one of the brokers TradingView shows you by default, and the login screen has a wrinkle about account types that trips people up. This guide walks through finding Vantage in TradingView's broker list, signing in to authorize the connection, and clearing the two errors people hit most often.

steps.heading: Open TradingView and load a chart
steps.body: Everything happens inside the normal TradingView chart workspace — there's no separate app or settings page to hunt for. In this example the chart is loaded to Gold Spot / U.S. Dollar (XAUUSD) on the OANDA feed, with the watchlist docked on the right showing indices like SPX and NDQ alongside individual stocks. The toolbar along the bottom of the window — the row with the magnifying glass, gear, and camera icons — is also home to the panel that manages broker connections, so it's worth having a chart open before you go looking for it. You don't need to be on any particular symbol or timeframe to connect a broker; any live chart will do.

image.caption: TradingView's default chart workspace on the OANDA gold feed, with the watchlist panel open on the right — this is the workspace the broker connection lives inside.

steps.heading: Open the Trading Panel and check the broker list
steps.body: Below the chart, click over to the Trading Panel tab next to Pine Editor. TradingView surfaces a short row of featured brokers here — in this case Share.Market, Paytm Money, and Motilal Oswal, each shown with a star rating — plus a "Show all brokers" button and a "Need a broker?" link for people without one yet. Vantage doesn't appear in that featured row, which is exactly the moment people assume it isn't supported and give up. It is supported; it's just one entry among the full list rather than one of the handful TradingView promotes by default.

image.caption: The Trading Panel tab at the bottom of the chart, showing a few featured brokers and a "Show all brokers" button. Vantage isn't one of the three shown here by default.

steps.heading: Search for Vantage in the full broker list
steps.body: Click "Show all brokers" to open the complete directory, then search or scroll to Vantage. Selecting it hands you off to Vantage's own connection page rather than keeping you inside TradingView, which is normal — every broker integration works this way, since the login itself has to happen on the broker's side. On mobile the same connection lives behind the broker icon in the chart toolbar instead of a Trading Panel tab, but it leads to the same search-and-select flow.

steps.heading: Sign in to your Vantage account to authorize the link
steps.body: Vantage opens a "Live Accounts" login screen asking for the email and password on your Vantage account. Enter your Vantage credentials as normal — this is the same login you'd use on Vantage's own site, not a separate TradingView password. The page also flags something worth reading before you type anything: connecting requires a "Vantage TradingView" account type specifically, so if you signed up for a standard Vantage account without picking that type, you may need to open a new one or convert your existing account first. There's also a confirmation that you've read Vantage's warning and terms of use, which you're agreeing to by clicking Connect.

image.caption: Vantage's Live Accounts login screen, reached after choosing Vantage from the broker list. It asks for your Vantage email and password and notes you'll need a "Vantage TradingView" account type to connect.

steps.heading: Choose a demo or live account
steps.body: Vantage lets you connect either a demo account for practice or a live account for real trading, and the login screen doesn't force one over the other — it depends on which set of credentials you enter. If you're setting this up for the first time, connecting the demo account first is the safer move: it proves the whole chain works — login, authorization, balance sync — before any real money is on the line.

steps.heading: Verify the connection and test it
steps.body: Once you click Connect, head back to TradingView's Trading Panel and confirm the broker status now shows connected rather than the earlier list of options. Your account balance and available leverage should appear in the panel, pulled live from Vantage. Before trading normally, place one small test trade directly from the chart and watch that it fills and that the balance updates — that single test catches most connection problems immediately instead of during a real trade later.

steps.heading: Fix the two most common connection errors
steps.body: "Broker not available in region" usually means Vantage's TradingView integration isn't offered for the country tied to your account, which is a Vantage policy rather than something you can configure around — check with Vantage support if you believe your region should be supported. "Failed to connect account" more often comes down to credentials or account type: double-check you're using your current Vantage login, and confirm the account you're connecting is actually the "Vantage TradingView" type mentioned on the login screen. Logging out of Vantage, logging back in, and retrying the connection from TradingView's broker list resolves most cases of this second error.

faq.question: Why does TradingView say Vantage is not available in my region?
faq.answer: This error usually relates to regional restrictions on certain broker integrations, so it's worth confirming Vantage supports your account's region before troubleshooting further.

faq.question: Can I connect both a demo and live Vantage account to TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView supports connecting either account type, so you can test with a demo account before switching to live trading.

faq.question: Will my account balance update in real time once connected?
faq.answer: Once the connection is verified, TradingView should reflect real-time balance and leverage updates from your linked Vantage account.

faq.question: What should I do if TradingView fails to connect my Vantage account?
faq.answer: Double-check your login credentials and account verification status on Vantage, then retry the authorization step in TradingView's broker panel.

faq.question: Do I need a special Vantage account to connect to TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes — Vantage's connection screen notes you need a "Vantage TradingView" account type. A standard Vantage account may need to be converted or a new one opened before the link will work.
